es: Organizar un viaje en un chat con personas de distintos países, aclarar malentendidos de vocabulario y confirmar el plan.

vocabulary.es: de acuerdo, con la misma idea

teaching.en: A small misunderstanding about a word such as boot or flat is easy to clarify if you ask politely and never suggest that anybody is wrong.
teaching.es: Un pequeño malentendido sobre una palabra como «boot» o «flat» es fácil de aclarar si preguntas con educación y nunca das a entender que alguien se equivoca.
teaching.explanationEs: Misunderstanding = malentendido; clarify = aclarar sin culpar.
segments: A small misunderstanding about a word such as boot or flat is easy
to clarify if you ask politely and never suggest that anybody is wrong.
teaching.audioText: A small misunderstanding about a word such as boot or flat is easy to clarify if you ask politely and never suggest that anybody is wrong.

teaching.en: Before we meet up in Dublin, let us agree on the plan: arrival on Friday, a flat near the centre, and a car for the whole weekend.
teaching.es: Antes de reunirnos en Dublín, pongámonos de acuerdo en el plan: llegada el viernes, un apartamento cerca del centro y un coche para todo el fin de semana.
teaching.explanationEs: Meet up = reunirse, encontrarse; plan = lo que se acuerda hacer.
segments: Before we meet up in Dublin, let us agree on the plan: arrival on
Friday, a flat near the centre, and a car for the whole weekend.

teaching.en: We spent the evening trying to iron out the last details of the plan, and by midnight everybody seemed to be on the same page.
teaching.es: Pasamos la noche intentando resolver los últimos detalles del plan, y a medianoche todos parecían estar de acuerdo.
teaching.explanationEs: Iron out = limar los últimos detalles; on the same page = tener la misma idea.
segments: We spent the evening trying to iron out the last details of the
plan, and by midnight everybody seemed to be on the same page.
teaching.audioText: We spent the evening trying to iron out the last details of the plan, and by midnight everybody seemed to be on the same page.

teaching.en: I cannot confirm the hotel yet, but I will get back to you by noon tomorrow, once the manager has answered my email.
teaching.es: Todavía no puedo confirmar el hotel, pero te responderé mañana antes del mediodía, cuando el gerente haya contestado mi correo.
teaching.explanationEs: Confirm = confirmar; get back to + persona = volver a contactar con ella.
segments: I cannot confirm the hotel yet, but I will get back to
you by noon tomorrow, once the manager has answered my email.

teaching.en: Just to be clear, the plan is to leave at nine; if everybody replies sounds good or that works for me, we can wrap up the discussion.
teaching.es: Para que quede claro, el plan es salir a las nueve; si todos responden «suena bien» o «me viene bien», podemos cerrar la conversación.
teaching.explanationEs: Just to be clear introduce un resumen; sounds good y that works for me aceptan una propuesta; wrap up = cerrar.

prompt.es: Elige la respuesta que aclara el malentendido sin culpar a Mia.

choices.text: Everybody knows that boot is the British word for the trunk, so please check again.
I am afraid that boot is an old word, so you may find it in books but nowhere else.
In Britain we call the trunk of the car the boot. Does that make sense?

feedback.es: Da el equivalente de cada variedad y termina con una pregunta cortés, sin hacer sentir a Mia que se equivoca ni restar valor a la palabra.

hint.es: Busca la respuesta que explica la palabra y mantiene un tono amable.

origin.text: Tom: 'I will pick you both up at five, and we can put the bags in the boot.' Mia: 'Sorry, what do you mean by boot? Is that a part of the car?'

prompt.es: Completa: «Para que quede claro, nos vemos a las cinco frente al hotel.»

accepted: clear

feedback.es: Just to be clear introduce un resumen final que elimina cualquier duda sobre el plan.

hint.es: Es el adjetivo que significa que algo no deja dudas.

origin.text: The plan has changed twice this week, and Mia is worried that somebody will go to the wrong place. So Sara writes: 'Just to be ___, we meet outside the hotel at five.'

prompt.es: Ordena: «Te responderé mañana sobre la hora.»

answer.text: I will get back to you about the time tomorrow

feedback.es: Get back to + persona significa volver a contactar con ella; about the time indica el asunto.

hint.es: Empieza por I will y termina con el momento.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige cómo resolvió la narradora el lío del chat.

choices.text: She explained each regional word and repeated the plan.
She asked everyone to write only in neutral words.
She called the group to cancel the weekend.

feedback.es: Explicó arvo y fortnight y repitió el plan con just to be clear; no pidió escribir distinto ni canceló nada.

origin.audio: Our group chat was a mess on Tuesday. My friend from Sydney said she would call this arvo, my cousin from Boston asked whether arvo meant tomorrow, and my flatmate from Leeds kept talking about a fortnight. In the end I wrote a short message: just to be clear, arvo is the afternoon, a fortnight is two weeks, and we will meet up on Friday at six.

choices.text: That she could not hear Tom on the call.
That she had only guessed what fortnight meant.
That she could not stay for two weeks.

feedback.es: Mia confiesa en el chat que adivinó fortnight por el contexto; no hubo problema de sonido ni de fechas.

origin.audio: During the call, Tom said he could stay for a fortnight. Mia nodded, but afterwards she admitted in the chat that she had only guessed the meaning from the context. Tom explained it cheerfully: a fortnight is two weeks. When Leo then suggested meeting this arvo to go through the route, Mia asked at once what arvo meant, and everybody laughed, including Leo.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué sugiere la reacción de Mia ante «arvo».

choices.text: She has become too embarrassed to admit when she does not follow.
She already knew what arvo meant and only wanted to check that Leo did.
She has learned to ask at once when a regional word is unclear.

feedback.es: Pregunta enseguida por arvo, a diferencia de lo que hizo con fortnight: ha aprendido a aclarar sin miedo; nadie se ofende y todos se ríen.

origin.audio: During the call, Tom said he could stay for a fortnight. Mia nodded, but afterwards she admitted in the chat that she had only guessed the meaning from the context. Tom explained it cheerfully: a fortnight is two weeks. When Leo then suggested meeting this arvo to go through the route, Mia asked at once what arvo meant, and everybody laughed, including Leo.

prompt.es: Completa: «No estoy seguro de que tengamos la misma idea del horario.»

accepted: page

feedback.es: On the same page significa compartir la misma información o idea sobre un asunto.

origin.text: The messages in the chat all say different things, and I am not sure we are all on the same ___ about the schedule, so let me write everything down.

prompt.es: Escribe tu mensaje al chat: aclara dos palabras y confirma el plan.

answer.text: Hi everyone, let me clarify two words before we finish the plan. Mia, in Britain the boot is what you call the trunk of the car, so Tom will put the bags there. Leo comes from Australia, and arvo is his word for the afternoon, so this arvo simply means this afternoon. Sorry for that, it was only a small misunderstanding. Just to be clear, we will meet up on Saturday at five outside the hotel. Tom will drive, and he will pick up Mia first, which is easier for everyone. If you are happy, please reply with sounds good or that works for me, and I will wrap up the plan tonight. I will also double check the hotel and get back to you by noon tomorrow. Cheers, Ana
accepted: Hi everyone, let me clarify two words before we finish the plan. Mia, in Britain the boot is what you call the trunk of the car, so Tom will put the bags there. Just to be clear, we will meet up on Saturday at five outside the hotel. Tom will drive, and he will pick up Mia first, which is easier for everyone. If you are happy, please reply with sounds good or that works for me, and I will wrap up the plan tonight. I will also double check the hotel and get back to you by noon tomorrow. Cheers, Ana

Hello all, I would like to clear up two words so that we are all on the same page. Mia, what Tom calls the boot is the trunk of the car, so that is where the bags will go. Leo is Australian, and arvo is his short word for afternoon, so this arvo means this afternoon. Sorry about the misunderstanding, it is easy to iron out. Just to be clear, we meet up at five on Saturday outside the hotel. Tom is driving, and he will pick up Mia first. Please tell me whether that works for you, and I will wrap up the plan tonight. I will also check the hotel and get back to you by noon tomorrow. Thanks, Ana

feedback.es: Un buen mensaje aclara las dos palabras con su equivalente, resume la hora y el lugar del plan y pide una respuesta sin culpar a nadie.

origin.text: Chat: Tom (Londres) dice que recogerá a todos y pondrá las bolsas en el «boot»; Mia (Boston) no entiende esa palabra. Leo (Sídney) propone ver la ruta «this arvo» y Mia tampoco sabe qué es. Plan: reunirse el sábado a las cinco frente al hotel. Escribe tu mensaje al grupo: aclara las dos palabras con su equivalente, confirma el plan y pide que respondan.

prompt.es: Lee el chat. ¿Qué da a entender Sara con su última respuesta?

origin.text: Sara: 'I will sort out the hotel and get back to you by noon.' Mia: 'Great, but is it a flat or only a room?' Sara: 'Good question. Let me iron out the details first, and I will confirm everything tonight.'

feedback.es: Iron out se usa con detalles o problemas pequeños que se resuelven; el pasivo necesita el participio ironed.
